summary.en: President Salva Kiir lifted the state of emergency in four states ahead of the 2027 elections while ethnic violence erupted in Wau town and clashes in Lakes State left seven dead. Gunmen opened fire on a Juba-Mundri vehicle, injuring two passengers. The UN warned that hunger is worsening sharply because of conflict and El Niño, and survivors of gender-based violence still lack essential medical care, exemplified by a rape victim walking four hours for treatment. South Sudan is pursuing a trade and investment hub role and has partnered with Israel's Gilat to launch nationwide satellite internet. 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: President Salva Kiir opphevet unntakstilstanden i fire delstater før valget i 2027, mens etnisk vold brøt ut i byen Wau og kamper i Lakes State førte til syv døde. Skytevåpen åpnet ild mot et kjøretøy på Juba-Mundri-ruten, og to passasjerer ble skadet. FN advarte om at sulten forverres kraftig på grunn av konflikt og El Niño, og overlevende av kjønnsbasert vold mangler fortsatt nødvendig medisinsk behandling, som eksemplifisert av en voldtektsoffer som gikk fire timer for å få behandling. Sør-Sudan satser på en rolle som handel‑ og investeringsknutepunkt og har inngått samarbeid med Israels Gilat for å lansere landsdekkende satellittinternett. 2 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
